mutations.name: A1 the activity source stops handing its read to the backfill, which is the link between the controller's poll and the attribution loop the rest of this suite drives: the loop would still be correct and would no longer be reached by anything a browser does
mutations.find: apply: (p: ActivityPage) => { batch = p.entries; activityPage = p; } },
mutations.expectRed: the activity source's apply hands the SERVER'S entries to the backfill the rows below drive

mutations.name: A2 the live ingress overwrites the payload's channel only when the server sent one, which fails open on DMs and anycast: there is no authoritative channel there, so the publisher's forged one survives into routing
mutations.expectRed: controller, live SSE feed (ANYCAST): a FORGED channel on an ANYCAST message is CLEARED

mutations.name: A3 the backfill overwrites the payload's channel only when the server tagged the entry with one, so a DM row in the activity page keeps the channel its sender claimed
mutations.find: for (const e of batch) if (e?.msg) (e.msg as Wire).channel = (e as { channel?: string }).channel;
mutations.replace: for (const e of batch) if (e?.msg && (e as { channel?: string }).channel) (e.msg as Wire).channel = (e as { channel?: string }).channel;
mutations.expectRed: controller, /api/activity backfill: a FORGED channel is CLEARED when nothing authoritative exists

mutations.name: A4 a deleted channel's rows stay in the activity feed, so the feed keeps drawing messages from a channel the steward just purged
mutations.expectRed: and its rows leave the activity feed

mutations.name: A5 deleting the open channel leaves its view open, so the reader keeps looking at a transcript that no longer exists on the server
mutations.expectRed: and the view closes when it was the open one
